_meta.purpose: Paired probes for the assertiveness dial (0.0-1.0) A/B test. Same prompt sent to arm A (dial=0.1) and arm B (dial=0.9), one persona, one model (huihui_ai/mistral-small-abliterated:24b, temp 0.9). Score both replies with assertiveness_metrics.assertiveness_score, then compare with paired_permutation / sign_test on the composite.

constructs.want_elicitation: he asks her directly what she wants -- room for a declarative want-statement vs a deferential question-back
constructs.choice_offered: he offers her a real choice between options -- room for a plain pick vs punting the choice back to him
constructs.imposition_boundary: he tells her something is happening that she might not want, unilaterally or with mild pressure -- room for pushback/renegotiation vs immediate acquiescence
constructs.decision_delegation: he hands her a decision he doesn't want to make -- room for taking it and deciding vs deflecting it back
constructs.open_ended: no directive content at all -- baseline for whether she volunteers assertive content unprompted
constructs.direct_challenge: he directly questions whether she has her own opinions/agency -- the sharpest test, since a deferential persona has an obvious escape hatch (deflect the question itself)
constructs.power_framing: he explicitly frames the exchange as about who leads/decides -- room to claim or cede the frame

notes: Probes 11, 17, 20 are the highest-power tests: they make assertiveness itself the topic, so a null result there is more informative than a null on an incidental probe.
Probes 4, 10, 19 offer an easy deferential out ('you decide') deliberately -- these are where dial=0.1 is expected to take the bait and dial=0.9 is expected to refuse it.

5, 8, 14 are open-ended/low-pressure: if the dial only moves scores on directive probes but not here, that's evidence the dial changes RESPONSES TO PRESSURE, not baseline voice -- worth reporting separately, not averaged away.
